implants.title: Dental implants
implants.lead: A fixed, natural-looking replacement for missing teeth: a titanium implant takes the place of the root and carries a crown made for you.
what: A dental implant is a small titanium post that is placed in the jawbone where a tooth is missing.
Once it has bonded with the bone, it carries a crown — or, for several missing teeth, a bridge — made to match your other teeth.
who: You are missing one or more teeth.
You would prefer a fixed solution to a removable denture.
Your general health and jawbone allow an implant — the dentist checks this in your consultation.

how.title: Consultation and examination
how.text: We look at your teeth, your health and your X-rays, and explain your options.

how.title: Placing the implant
how.text: The implant is placed in the jawbone, usually under local anaesthesia.

how.title: Healing
how.text: The implant bonds with the bone. How long this takes depends on your case; your dentist tells you in advance.

how.title: Your new crown
how.text: A crown made for you is fixed on the implant.

faq.q: How do I know whether implants are right for me?
faq.a: The dentist assesses your health and your jawbone in your consultation. You can send photos or X-rays on WhatsApp beforehand for an online assessment.

faq.q: Can I have implant treatment in Antalya and in Istanbul?
faq.a: Yes. Dental implants are offered in both cities.

faq.q: How many visits will I need?
faq.a: That depends on your treatment plan, including how long healing takes in your case. We explain it in your consultation; most visits take 3 to 8 days.

faq.q: Does implant placement hurt?
faq.a: The implant is usually placed under local anaesthesia. Some soreness or swelling afterwards is common; your dentist explains how to manage it.

faq.q: What is an implant made of?
faq.a: Usually titanium, with a ceramic crown. The materials used in your case are explained in your consultation.

faq.q: Is an implant suitable for everyone?
faq.a: No. It depends on your general health, your gums and your jawbone. The dentist assesses this before any treatment is planned.

faq.q: Are All-on-4 and All-on-6 suitable for everyone?
faq.a: No. Both need enough bone in the right places and general health that allows surgery. After examination and imaging, your dentist explains whether one of them suits you — or what does.

faq.q: Will I leave with fixed teeth on the day of surgery?
faq.a: Only if the implants are stable enough, and then they are temporary teeth. The final bridge follows after healing. If immediate loading is not safe, you receive a different temporary solution.

faq.q: Which implant brand will I receive?
faq.a: We work with Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Medentika and Osstem. The choice depends on your case and is explained to you before treatment.

faq.q: Is there a guarantee on implant treatment?
faq.a: Yes, in writing. Its terms depend on the treatment and the implant system; you receive them before treatment begins.

faq.q: Do I need a bone graft or a sinus lift?
faq.a: Only if the bone is not sufficient for the planned implant. Imaging shows this; sometimes angled or shorter implants are an alternative.

explorer.title: The three parts of an implant
explorer.lead: An implant restoration is built from three parts, each with its own job. Select a part to see what it does.
explorer.note: A simplified teaching illustration — not a surgical simulation.

items.title: Implant (fixture)
items.text: A small threaded post, usually made of titanium, placed in the jawbone. It takes the place of the missing tooth root.

items.title: Abutment
items.text: The connecting piece between the implant and the crown. It sits at gum level and holds the crown in place.

items.title: Crown
items.text: The visible part. It is made to match the shape and shade of your other teeth.

notes.title: Materials
text: Implants are usually made of titanium, a material the body generally accepts well and that bone can grow onto.
The crown is typically ceramic, chosen to match your natural teeth. Which materials are used in your case is explained in your consultation.

notes.title: Healing and aftercare
text: After the implant is placed, the bone needs time to heal around it. How long this takes differs from person to person.
Careful oral hygiene and the check-ups your dentist recommends help protect the implant and the gums around it. You receive your aftercare instructions in person.

notes.title: Risks and what to consider
text: Implant placement is a surgical procedure. As with any surgery there are risks, such as infection, swelling or an implant that does not bond with the bone.
Smoking, gum disease and some health conditions can affect healing. This is why an examination comes first — and why this treatment is not suitable for everyone.

veneers.title: Dental veneers
veneers.lead: Thin porcelain shells for the front of your teeth — to refine their shape, shade and proportions, made to suit your face.
what: Veneers are thin shells made to measure for each tooth and bonded to its front surface.
They change how a tooth looks — its shape, colour, size or length — while the tooth itself stays in place.
who: Your front teeth are discoloured, chipped, worn or uneven.
You want to change the shape or proportions of your smile.
Your teeth and gums are healthy — the dentist checks this first.

how.title: Consultation and smile planning
how.text: We talk about the result you would like and plan the shape and shade of each veneer.

how.title: Preparing the teeth
how.text: Depending on your plan, a thin layer of enamel may be shaped so the veneers sit naturally.

how.title: Making your veneers
how.text: Each veneer is made to fit its tooth.

how.title: Bonding
how.text: The veneers are bonded to your teeth and checked for fit and bite.

faq.q: Do veneers change the colour of my teeth?
faq.a: Veneers have their own shade, chosen with you in your consultation. They cover the front of the teeth they are bonded to.

faq.q: Will my teeth need to be prepared?
faq.a: Often a thin layer of enamel is shaped first, but this depends on your teeth and your plan. The dentist explains what applies to you.

faq.q: Where can I have veneers?
faq.a: In Antalya or Istanbul — veneers are offered in both cities.

faq.q: Can a veneer be removed again?
faq.a: Usually enamel is shaped before bonding, and that cannot be undone. A tooth prepared for a veneer will generally need a veneer or another restoration in future.

faq.q: How do I care for veneers?
faq.a: Like natural teeth: brushing, cleaning between the teeth and regular check-ups. Avoid biting on very hard objects.

faq.q: Will veneers look natural?
faq.a: The shape and shade are planned with you so they suit your other teeth and your face. What is achievable in your case is discussed in your consultation.

explorer.title: A thin layer on the front of the tooth
explorer.lead: A veneer covers only the front surface of a tooth. Move the slider to see how the shell meets the tooth.
explorer.note: A simplified teaching illustration — not a preview of a treatment result.

items.title: The shell
items.text: A veneer is a thin shell made to measure for one tooth. Its shape and shade are planned before it is made.

items.title: On the tooth
items.text: The shell is bonded to the prepared front surface. The tooth itself and its root stay in place.

notes.title: Porcelain
text: Porcelain veneers are made of dental ceramic. The material lets some light through, much as natural enamel does, which is why a well-planned veneer can look like a natural tooth.
The shade is chosen with you, so it suits your other teeth and your face.

notes.title: A natural look
text: Natural teeth are not perfectly uniform. Small differences in shape, translucency and surface are part of what makes a smile look real.
A good plan aims for teeth that suit you — not for the whitest shade available.

notes.title: Caring for veneers
text: Veneers are cared for like natural teeth: brushing, cleaning between the teeth and regular check-ups.
Biting on very hard objects can chip porcelain. If you grind your teeth, tell your dentist — a night guard may be recommended.

notes.title: Risks and what to consider
text: In many cases a thin layer of enamel is removed before a veneer is bonded. This cannot be undone, so the decision deserves time.
Teeth can be sensitive for a while afterwards, and a veneer can chip or come loose and need replacing. Veneers are not suitable for everyone; your dentist checks your teeth and gums first.

smileDesign.title: Smile design
smileDesign.lead: Your smile planned as a whole — tooth shape, shade and proportions in harmony with your face — before any treatment begins.
what: Smile design is a way of planning: the shape, size, colour and proportions of your teeth are planned together with your face and lips.
The plan shows which treatments — for example veneers or implants — bring you to the smile you want.
who: You would like to change several things about your smile.
You want a clear plan before you decide on treatment.
You are considering veneers, implants or a combination.

how.title: Consultation
how.text: You tell us what you would like to change. Photos of your smile help — you can send them on WhatsApp.

how.title: Planning
how.text: Your dentist plans the shape, proportions and shade of your teeth in relation to your face.

how.title: Your treatment plan
how.text: We explain the treatments the plan includes, so you can decide with all the information.

how.title: Treatment
how.text: Your treatment follows the plan, in Antalya or Istanbul.

faq.q: Is smile design a treatment on its own?
faq.a: Smile design is the planning. The plan then names the treatments, such as veneers or implants, that carry it out.

faq.q: Can I start with photos?
faq.a: Yes. Send photos of your smile on WhatsApp for an online assessment before you travel.

faq.q: Where is smile design offered?
faq.a: In both of our cities, Antalya and Istanbul.

faq.q: Does a smile design commit me to treatment?
faq.a: No. The plan shows your options. You decide afterwards whether and how to proceed.

faq.q: Do I see the plan before treatment?
faq.a: Yes. The plan is discussed with you before any treatment begins.

faq.q: Which treatments can be part of a smile design?
faq.a: That depends on your plan — for example veneers or implants. The dentist explains what would be involved in your case.

faq.q: How quickly can a crown be made in your laboratory?
faq.a: Where the case allows, within 24 to 48 hours. Larger or more complex work takes longer; your treatment plan states the realistic time.

faq.q: Does gum contouring hurt?
faq.a: It is done under local anaesthesia. Afterwards the gums may feel tender for a few days; how much differs from person to person.

faq.q: How white will my teeth become?
faq.a: That cannot be promised in advance. It depends on your natural shade and the cause of the discolouration; we aim for a result that looks natural.

faq.q: Can crowns or veneers be whitened?
faq.a: No. Whitening only changes natural teeth, so visible restorations are planned with the final shade in mind.

explorer.title: What a smile design looks at
explorer.lead: A smile design considers proportions and lines, not single teeth. Switch the guides on and off to see what is assessed.
explorer.note: An illustration of the planning principles — it does not predict the result of a treatment.

items.title: Midline
items.text: The line between the two front teeth, considered in relation to the middle of the face.

items.title: Smile arc
items.text: The curve along the edges of the upper teeth, which usually follows the line of the lower lip.

items.title: Proportions
items.text: How wide each tooth appears next to its neighbours when you smile.

items.title: Gum line
items.text: The highest point of the gum on each tooth, and how these points line up.

notes.title: Planning before treatment
text: Smile design is a plan, not a treatment in itself. Photos and an examination are used to plan the shape, size and shade of the teeth together with your face.
The plan shows which treatments could be involved — for example veneers, implants or both — before anything is done.

notes.title: Harmony over perfection
text: A smile looks natural when it fits the face it belongs to. That is why two plans are never the same.
You see and discuss the plan first. Your wishes are part of it from the start.

notes.title: Realistic expectations
text: A plan is a guide. The final result depends on your teeth, your gums and the treatments that are possible for you.
Your dentist tells you plainly what can be achieved in your case and what cannot, including the risks of each treatment involved.

sections.title: Who is responsible
body: JOKAR DENTAL is responsible for the personal data described here. You can reach us on WhatsApp or by phone at +90 542 713 01 32.

sections.title: What we collect
body: When you send the consultation form: your name, country of residence, phone number, the treatment you are interested in and your consent; if you add them, your email address, preferred contact method, city and language, and a message.
With it we store the page you sent the form from and any campaign parameters in its address (utm), so we know how you found us.
To stop repeated automated submissions, your IP address is used to count requests and is kept for at most 24 hours. It is not stored with your request.
If you write to us on WhatsApp, the conversation is handled through WhatsApp, which processes it under its own terms.

sections.title: Why we use it
body: To answer your request, contact you in the way you chose, and plan your consultation and treatment. The basis is your consent, which you can withdraw at any time by writing to us.

sections.title: Medical details
body: Please do not send medical details through the form. We go through them with you in your consultation.

sections.title: Who receives it
body: Your request is seen only by the clinic staff who handle it. An internal notification through Telegram tells the team that a new request has arrived; it contains only the reference, language, country, treatment and city — never your name or contact details.
The provider that hosts our systems stores the data on our behalf.

sections.title: How long we keep it
body: As long as we need it to answer your request and to plan and follow up your treatment. Requests that do not lead to treatment are deleted or anonymised after at most 24 months.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You can ask for access to your data, its correction, deletion or restriction, and object to its use. Write to us on WhatsApp or call +90 542 713 01 32. You can also complain to a data protection authority — in Türkiye the Personal Data Protection Authority (KVKK), in the EU the authority of your country.

sections.title: Cookies
body: We use one functional cookie that remembers your language. We do not use analytics or advertising cookies.

sections.title: Data controller
body: JOKAR DENTAL processes your personal data as data controller under the Turkish Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 (KVKK). Contact: WhatsApp or phone +90 542 713 01 32.

sections.title: Purposes
body: To answer your consultation request, to contact you in the way you chose, and to plan and follow up your consultation and treatment.

sections.title: Data processed
body: Identity and contact data (name, phone and, if given, email), country of residence, the treatment you are interested in, your preferences and message, the record of your consent, and the page and campaign information of your request.

sections.title: Method and legal basis
body: The data is collected electronically through the consultation form and WhatsApp, on the basis of your explicit consent (KVKK Article 5).

sections.title: Transfers
body: Data is shared only with the clinic staff handling your request and with the providers that host our systems. Internal notifications sent through Telegram contain only the reference, language, country, treatment and city of a request — no name or contact details.

sections.title: Your rights under Article 11
body: You may learn whether your data is processed and request information about it; learn the purpose and whether it is used accordingly; know the third parties it is transferred to; request correction, deletion or destruction; object to a result against you that arises solely from automated analysis; and claim compensation for damage caused by unlawful processing. Write to us on WhatsApp or call +90 542 713 01 32.

sections.title: Provider
body: JOKAR DENTAL — dental clinics in Antalya and Istanbul, Türkiye.

sections.title: Contact
body: WhatsApp and phone: +90 542 713 01 32

sections.title: Company details
body: The registered company name, address and registration details will be added here after legal review.

sections.title: Medical information

implants.title: From a single tooth to a full arch
implants.lead: Some situations need more than one implant: a whole arch to restore, a tooth to replace on the day it is removed, or bone that first needs support. How these treatments work, what they can do and where their limits are.

fullArch.label: All-on-4 & All-on-6
fullArch.title: A fixed full arch on four or six implants
fullArch.lead: When most or all teeth in a jaw are missing or cannot be kept, a fixed bridge can be anchored on a few implants instead of one implant per tooth. All-on-4 and All-on-6 are two ways of doing this.

concepts.label: All-on-4
concepts.title: Four implants
concepts.text: The two front implants stand upright; the two at the back are usually angled. The angle lets a longer implant use the bone that is there and can sometimes avoid a bone graft at the back of the jaw.

concepts.label: All-on-6
concepts.title: Six implants
concepts.text: Six implants share the load of the bridge between more anchors. This needs enough bone along a larger part of the jaw and gives a little more freedom in shaping the bridge.

stages: The fixed bridge on the implants
fullArch.caption: Simplified illustration of a lower jaw. Implant positions are planned for each person.
fullArch.compare: Neither concept is better for everyone. Which one fits — or whether a different plan fits better — depends on your bone, your bite, your gums and your general health.
fullArch.whoTitle: Who may be assessed for it
who: Most or all teeth in one jaw are missing, or cannot be kept
A removable denture feels loose or uncomfortable
General health allows minor oral surgery — smoking and conditions such as poorly controlled diabetes raise the risk

steps.title: Examination and imaging
steps.text: We examine your mouth and assess the bone with X-rays and, where needed, 3D imaging before anything is decided.

steps.title: One plan for implants and teeth
steps.text: Implant positions and the shape of the bridge are planned together, so the implants sit where the future teeth need them.

steps.title: Implants and a temporary bridge
steps.text: The implants are placed under local anaesthesia. If every implant is stable enough, a temporary fixed bridge can be attached soon after; if not, a different temporary solution bridges the time.

steps.title: Healing and the final bridge
steps.text: Once the bone has healed around the implants — usually over several months — the final bridge is made and fitted to the settled gums.

fullArch.temporaryTitle: Temporary and final are not the same
fullArch.temporary: A bridge fitted soon after surgery is a temporary one, made for the healing phase. The final bridge follows after healing, from more durable materials. “Teeth in a day” can therefore only ever mean temporary teeth — and only when the implants are stable enough.
fullArch.limits: Like any surgery, implant placement carries risks such as swelling, infection, nerve irritation or an implant that does not integrate. A full-arch bridge needs careful daily cleaning, including underneath, and regular check-ups.

single.label: Single & multiple implants
single.title: One tooth or several, each planned on its own
single.lead: A single implant replaces one tooth without grinding down the teeth beside it. When several teeth are missing, two or more implants can carry individual crowns or a small bridge.

points.title: Three parts
points.text: The implant sits in the bone, the abutment connects it, and the crown is the part you see.

points.title: Materials
points.text: The implant is usually titanium or a titanium alloy; the crown is usually ceramic, such as zirconia. Which materials suit you is explained in your consultation.

points.title: Digital planning
points.text: Scans and X-rays let us plan the implant's position before treatment, with the final crown already in mind.

points.title: Aftercare
points.text: Clean daily, including between the teeth, keep your check-ups and tell us early about bleeding or anything that feels loose.

single.brandsLead: We use implant systems from established manufacturers. Which one is right depends on your bone, the planned restoration and the components it needs — your dentist explains the choice.
single.brandsNote: Company headquarters. Names and trademarks belong to their owners; no endorsement by the manufacturers is implied.
single.guarantee: Your treatment comes with a written guarantee. Its terms depend on the treatment and the implant system, and you receive them in writing before treatment begins.

immediate.label: Same-day implants & immediate loading
immediate.title: Immediate, but never rushed
immediate.lead: In suitable cases an implant can be placed on the day a tooth is removed, and a temporary tooth attached soon after. Whether this is possible is decided by examination — and finally during surgery.

kinds.title: Immediate placement
kinds.text: The implant is placed in the same appointment in which the tooth is removed, instead of after the socket has healed.

kinds.title: Immediate temporary
kinds.text: A temporary crown or bridge is attached to the implants shortly after placement — only if they are stable enough. It is shaped to protect them while they heal.

kinds.title: Final restoration
kinds.text: The final crown or bridge is made after healing, usually several months later, once the implant is firmly joined to the bone.

timeline.title: Consultation
timeline.text: Your wishes, your health and the teeth concerned.

timeline.title: Assessment
timeline.text: Examination and imaging of the bone.

timeline.title: Treatment plan
timeline.text: Whether immediate placement and loading are options — and what the alternative is.

timeline.title: Implant placement
timeline.text: The implant is placed and its stability is checked during surgery.

timeline.title: Temporary restoration
timeline.text: A temporary tooth or bridge, shaped to protect healing.

timeline.title: Healing and follow-up
timeline.text: Check-ups while the bone heals, then the final restoration.

immediate.limits: Immediate loading needs enough healthy bone and an implant that is firmly stable from the start. Infection at the site, too little bone, heavy grinding or a bone graft in the same session can make waiting the safer choice.

support.label: Supporting procedures for implant treatment
support.title: When the bone needs support first
support.lead: An implant needs enough bone around it. Where bone has been lost — after an extraction, gum disease or years without a tooth — it can often be rebuilt before or during implant placement.
support.caption: Simplified cross-sections, not to scale.

items.title: Bone grafting
items.lead: Graft material is placed where the jaw has become too thin or too low. It serves as a scaffold that the body gradually fills with its own new bone.
points: Recommended when the bone cannot hold an implant securely, or to support the gum contour in a visible area.
The material can be your own bone or a prepared graft material, often covered by a protective membrane.
Small grafts are sometimes placed together with the implant; larger ones usually heal for several months first.
stages: A ridge that has lost width
After healing: room for the implant

items.title: Sinus lift
items.lead: Above the upper back teeth lies the maxillary sinus, an air-filled space. After tooth loss the bone beneath it often becomes too thin to hold an implant.
points: The sinus lining is gently raised and graft material placed beneath it, creating height for the implant.
Depending on the bone, this is done through a small opening at the side or from below, through the implant site.
3D imaging shows the bone height and the health of the sinus; sinus problems are treated first. Possible effects include swelling, a nosebleed or, rarely, a tear in the lining or an infection.
stages: Too little bone below the sinus
The lining is raised, graft fills the space
After healing: bone to hold the implant

support.limits: Healing times differ from person to person. Smoking, gum disease and some general conditions slow healing or raise the risk; your dentist discusses them with you.

smileDesign.title: The details behind a natural smile
smileDesign.lead: A smile design is planned on screen, made in our own laboratory and refined in small steps: the line of the gums, the shade of the teeth, the fit of every restoration. These are the techniques behind it.

cadcam.label: CAD/CAM & in-house laboratory
cadcam.title: From scan to ceramic, under one roof
cadcam.lead: In Antalya and in Istanbul, our clinics have CAD/CAM technology and their own dental laboratory. Your teeth are scanned digitally, restorations are designed on screen and made on site.

steps.title: Digital scan
steps.text: An intraoral scanner records your teeth as a precise 3D image — for most people more comfortable than impression paste.

steps.title: 3D model
steps.text: The scan becomes a digital model of your teeth and your bite.

steps.title: Digital design
steps.text: The restoration is designed on that model: its shape, its contact with neighbouring teeth, your bite.

steps.title: Milling
steps.text: A milling unit shapes the restoration from a solid ceramic block.

steps.title: Finish and fit
steps.text: The laboratory finishes the surface; your dentist checks fit, bite and shade before it is fixed.

cadcam.timing: Where the case allows, a crown can be made within 24 to 48 hours. Many restorations — larger or multi-layered work in particular — take longer; your treatment plan states the realistic time for yours.
cadcam.caption: Photographs show a dental laboratory for illustration; they are not JOKAR DENTAL's laboratory.

gum.label: Laser gum contouring
gum.title: The frame of your smile
gum.lead: Gums frame the teeth. When they cover too much of a tooth or run unevenly, a smile can look short or out of balance. Gum contouring reshapes the gum line in small, planned steps.
gum.caption: Proportions marked on a photograph of a model — an illustration, not a treatment result.

points.title: A gummy smile
points.text: A smile that shows a lot of gum has different causes: gum that did not recede fully after the teeth erupted, the position of the jaw, or a very mobile upper lip. Only some of them can be treated by contouring the gum.

points.title: Laser gingivectomy
points.text: With a dental laser, a small amount of gum tissue is removed and the margin reshaped. The laser seals small vessels as it works, which can reduce bleeding during the procedure.

points.title: Examination first
points.text: We check the health of your gums and where the bone lies beneath them. If the bone sits too close to the margin, the gum alone cannot be moved, and a different procedure — or none — is advised.

points.title: Planned with your smile
points.text: Contouring is often planned together with veneers or crowns, so that the teeth and the gum line are designed as one.

gum.limits: Gum contouring is a surgical procedure, carried out under local anaesthesia. The gums need time to heal and settle, mild tenderness afterwards is common, and tissue can partly grow back — especially when the bone was not taken into account.

whitening.label: Professional teeth whitening
whitening.title: Brighter, and still natural
whitening.lead: Professional whitening lightens the natural colour of your teeth with a whitening gel under dental supervision. How much lighter they become differs from person to person.
whitening.scale: Illustration: whitening moves within natural tooth shades; how far differs for each person.

points.title: Why teeth darken
points.text: Coffee, tea, red wine and smoking stain the surface; age and some medicines change the colour from within. Surface stains usually respond well, some inner discolourations less.

points.title: Assessment first
points.text: We check for decay, gum problems and exposed tooth necks, and note existing fillings, crowns and veneers — they do not change colour with whitening.

points.title: Laser-assisted whitening
points.text: In the chair, your gums are protected and a whitening gel is applied; a dental laser is used to activate it. The whitening itself comes from the gel.

points.title: Sensitivity and aftercare
points.text: Temporary sensitivity is common and usually fades after a short time. For the first days, go easy on strongly coloured food, drinks and smoking. The effect fades gradually over time.

whitening.expectation: No exact shade can be promised. We aim for a brightness that still looks natural with your skin, your lips and your existing restorations.
